title: The Star That Vanished from Every Telescope—Except One
hook: A star in a distant galaxy blinked out of existence, but one observatory kept tracking it—and what it saw defies physics.
why_this_can_go_viral: The mystery of something vanishing from sight but not from reality triggers deep unease and curiosity—perfect for doomscrolling.

title: The Secret 1980s Program That Tracked an Alien Fleet
hook: Declassified documents reveal a U.S. intelligence program that monitored an incoming fleet of unknown objects—then suddenly stopped.
why_this_can_go_viral: Conspiracy + government secrecy + potential alien threat = viral fuel for the cosmic niche.

title: The Asteroid That Changed Earth's Rotation—Just Slightly
hook: A massive asteroid grazing Earth didn't hit, but its gravity pulled our planet's spin off by a fraction of a second forever.
why_this_can_go_viral: Tiny but permanent change to Earth triggers existential unease—viewers love 'almost ended the world' stories.

title: The Galaxy That Has a Void at Its Center—No Black Hole, Nothing
hook: Astronomers found a galaxy with a perfectly empty core—no supermassive black hole, no stars, just nothingness.
why_this_can_go_viral: A void in space where something should be is deeply unsettling—'nothing' is scarier than 'something'.

title: The Classified Plan to Nuke an Incoming Asteroid—And It Almost Happened
hook: In 1998, the U.S. had a secret contingency to detonate a nuclear warhead on an asteroid—the order was nearly given.
why_this_can_go_viral: Nuclear weapons + space threat = explosive mix. The 'almost happened' angle pumps urgency.

title: The Star That Erupted with a Shockwave—And It Traveled Faster Than Light
hook: A neutron star flared, and its shockwave appeared to break the speed of light—an illusion that hides something terrifying.
why_this_can_go_viral: Faster-than-light always sparks debate—the twist that it's an illusion makes it educational and eerie.

title: The Dark Matter That Strangled a Star—Invisible Noose
hook: A star collapsed for no reason—until researchers realized dark matter particles clumped inside it, crushing it from within.
why_this_can_go_viral: Dark matter as an active killer gives the invisible a menacing personality—highly shareable.

title: The Rogue Planet That Carried a Dead Star's Remains
hook: A planet drifting alone through space has a core made of neutron star material—a fragment from a supernova.
why_this_can_go_viral: Rogue planets are scary—this one carries the corpse of a star, making it a ghost world.

title: The Secret Space Shuttle That Spied on a Chinese Satellite—And Vanished
hook: A classified U.S. shuttle mission tracked a mysterious Chinese satellite—then both disappeared from radar for 3 days.
why_this_can_go_viral: Spy drama in space—disappearances fuel conspiracy theories and high retention.

title: The Supernova That Sent a Gamma Ray Burst—Straight Through Earth
hook: A gamma ray burst hit Earth in 774 AD—we know because ancient trees recorded it. The next one might not miss.
why_this_can_go_viral: Past events that could repeat are terrifying—'it happened before' adds credibility to the doom.

title: The Asteroid That Has a Metallic Core Worth More Than Earth's Economy
hook: A single asteroid contains enough platinum and gold to crash the world economy—and it's heading our way.
why_this_can_go_viral: Wealth + danger combo—viewers imagine both apocalypse and fortune.

title: The Dead Star That Sent a Pulse Every 2.5 Seconds—For 50 Years Straight
hook: A pulsar blinked like a cosmic lighthouse for half a century—then suddenly stopped. No one predicted it.
why_this_can_go_viral: Something that stops after half a century feels like a message ending—creates mystery.

title: The Classified Apollo 19 Mission—The One They Never Announced
hook: Records show a 19th Apollo mission was funded and crewed—then scrubbed. Whispers say it launched anyway.
why_this_can_go_viral: Secret Apollo mission is a conspiracy goldmine—extremely high curiosity and shareability.

title: The Extinction Event That Came from a Comet—Not an Asteroid
hook: The dinosaurs weren't killed by an asteroid. New evidence points to a comet that tore apart before impact.
why_this_can_go_viral: Challenging a well-known fact hooks viewers—'everything you know is wrong' angle.

title: The Star That Blinked in a Pattern—And It Spelled Out a Number
hook: A variable star dimmed in a sequence that matched prime numbers. Either coincidence or something sent it.
why_this_can_go_viral: Patterns in space feel like intelligence—prime numbers are a classic 'we are here' signal.

title: The Rogue Black Hole That's Drifting Toward the Milky Way
hook: A black hole ejected from its galaxy is heading our way—and when it arrives, it will tear the solar system apart.
why_this_can_go_viral: An unstoppable, invisible threat from deep space—pure existential horror.

title: The Dark Matter That Created a Ghost Galaxy—Visible Only in Infrared
hook: A galaxy made almost entirely of dark matter emits no light—but infrared telescopes revealed its haunting shape.
why_this_can_go_viral: A ghost in space—visual and emotional hook with a spooky aesthetic.

title: The Secret 1970s Program That Tried to Communicate with a Dead Satellite
hook: The USSR spent billions trying to re-contact a satellite that went silent—until it responded with a signal in a dead language.
why_this_can_go_viral: A response in a dead language is pure creepypasta fuel—highly viral.

title: The Comet That Entered the Solar System—And Brought Something Living
hook: Samples from a comet contained organic structures that resembled fossilized bacteria—from another star system.
why_this_can_go_viral: Life from another star system—both thrilling and terrifying. The 'invasion' angle is subtle but potent.
